amendment_authority: Founder explicitly requires plan update first; deliberate real requests for implementation verification, retain runaway/significant-accidental-spend safeguards without arbitrary tight caps/new hard spending approval gates; coordinator reviews before ce-work.
amendment_summary: Planning remains inspection/design; implementation live integration deliberately uses actual network/provider/model/QA requests.
Explicit paid legacy/full journey is permitted after target/account/data/provider checks; default discovery/build/harness remains protected.
Observe purpose/progress/available usage; retain first failure and diagnose before retry; stop/notify runaway/nonprogress/anomalous or unexpected cost without new caps/thresholds/quota tooling.
Keep live auth/streaming/persistence/reload coverage pending until actually performed; fixtures/503 do not substitute.
Separate production deployment/config/domain/access/write-scope authorization; preserve QA ownership/history, founder-record exclusion, privacy and optional safe1Password.
Coordinator timing clarifications integrated for cold-entry proof, config listing vs safe occupied-port preflight, and QA exclusion in existing selected cohort reports.

findings.title: Production-DB QA writes accumulate without containment
findings.section: KTD4 — Prefer controlled final-origin QA before invitations
findings.why_it_matters: The deployed lane (S3–S5) does real writes to the shared production database using the one QA account. Every release and every relevant change adds more additive mutations, and reset is forbidden. The plan assumes the account's checkpoint will keep supporting a meaningful saved turn and continuation. Over repeated releases the QA history drifts, and S4 can stop finding a legitimate next choice. Nothing in the plan covers what happens then, except that cleanup must not remove QA history. The plan should name an accepted limit: when the checkpoint can no longer support S3/S4, add another dedicated QA account rather than resetting the existing one.
findings.suggested_fix: In Assumptions, state that when the existing QA checkpoint can no longer support S3/S4 additively, the agent stops and requests a further dedicated QA account instead of resetting or skipping rows.
evidence: Public final-origin QA writes to a shared production database.
Do not reset it to manufacture a convenient journey.

findings.title: Cost-anomaly stop has no reference baseline
findings.section: KTD7 — Select a purpose, then observe progress and usage
findings.why_it_matters: Agents must stop on 'anomalous/unexpected cost', but the plan sets no expected per-scenario usage reference. This is not a cap, just a reference point. Without one, a cold agent can't tell normal deliberate spend from an anomaly. R9's spend protection then depends on each agent's own judgment and can fail silently. If the scenario matrix records the typical observed token/step usage per live row, agents get a reference point without adding a hard threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: In U2, have the scenario matrix record each live row's observed typical step/token usage from its first passing run as a non-binding reference for 'unexpected cost'.
evidence: stop/notify on nonprogressing repetition, runaway behavior or anomalous/unexpected cost
without arbitrary tight request caps or a new hard spending approval threshold

residual_risks: The production Google OAuth flow for the QA account may require interactive 2FA on each new session, so S2 cannot run without the founder present at every release.

findings.title: U3 test scenarios contradict on opt-in for discovery
findings.section: U3 — Bound and correct the legacy browser entrypoint
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers can't tell whether configuration discovery (e.g. `playwright test --list`) has to fail without the opt-in. KTD6 (explicit legacy browser run) requires the opt-in check to happen before server startup. But the second scenario only lists the suite when the opt-in is given. And the Verification section says to use 'safe configuration discovery' with no mention of the opt-in. If the opt-in guard lives in the config file, listing without it could also throw, which would break the safe discovery used elsewhere. The plan should say whether listing without the opt-in is allowed.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the opt-in guard runs at webServer/test startup, not at config load. Listing without the opt-in prints the missing-opt-in explanation and runs nothing.
evidence: Invoking without legacy opt-in fails clearly before starting a server/browser/provider request
With explicit opt-in, configuration discovery lists only the labelled legacy journey

findings.title: U1 cold-entry test depends on U2's later output
findings.section: U1 — Publish the discoverable verification entrypoint
findings.why_it_matters: U1's main test can't run until U2 has written the scenario matrix, yet U2 is listed as depending on U1. As written, U1 can't be confirmed done when it lands, and the Definition of Done item for U1 can't be checked on its own. Either move the cold-entry proof into U2's or U4's verification, or say clearly that U1's completion is confirmed after U2.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the six-change cold-entry scenario into U4's guide proof, and limit U1 verification to link/source review.
evidence: After U2 supplies the integrated matrix, a fresh read-only agent given only the repo entrypoint and six representative change descriptions finds the guide

residual_risks: Final-origin QA writes go to the shared production database, and the only protection is QA account ownership. If S5's interruption timing goes wrong, it could leave partial state in the founder-facing production data.
deferred_questions: Which local auth/data bootstrap counts as safe enough for the auth-enabled local Method integration lane in U4?

resolved_claims.claim: Production-DB QA writes accumulate without containment
resolved_claims.reason: Re-raises earlier speculative checkpoint exhaustion. Existing repeating Method supports continuation, and plan explicitly stops and presents an alternative if checkpoint inadequate. No actual exhausted checkpoint or founder-record write path is shown. Human approved additive QA and no reset; no new account lifecycle mechanism required.

resolved_claims.claim: Cost-anomaly stop has no reference baseline
resolved_claims.reason: KTD7 defines selected purpose/scope, progress and available usage observations, alongside existing runtime limits and diagnosis-before-retry. No established typical monetary baseline is available, and one passing run cannot establish typical cost. Recording a new per-row baseline would add calibration work without a demonstrated missing safeguard. Existing observations/receipts remain available as context without a new threshold/gate/tool.

resolved_claims.claim: U3 test scenarios contradict on opt-in for discovery
resolved_claims.reason: KTD6 and U3 explicitly require opt-in before startup, default invocation fails before any paid action, and listing with explicit opt-in is a separate safe discovery test. Verification cites those scenarios; it never promises listing without opt-in. Suggested no-opt-in listing is an alternative mechanism rather than a demonstrated contradiction.

resolved_claims.claim: U1 cold-entry test depends on U2's later output
resolved_claims.reason: Coordinator specifically directed integrated-matrix timing; amended scenario explicitly says After U2 supplies the integrated matrix. U4 then proves the combined kit after U1–U3. The review itself offers this timing clarification as a valid remedy, which is already present. No instruction claims premature final acceptance of U1.

resolved_claims.claim: Google security barriers can remain founder-dependent
resolved_claims.reason: R6/Access retain encountered security steps as human work; no unattended sign-in promise.

resolved_claims.claim: S5 partial production state could affect founder-facing data
resolved_claims.reason: Dedicated QA ownership, no founder records, canonical atomic/cancellation checks and saved-state truth remain active. No cross-account or founder-data contamination path is demonstrated. Intentional interrupted QA state is an explicit test outcome requiring reconciliation, not a new permission to modify founder data.

resolved_claims.claim: Which local auth/data bootstrap is safe enough?
resolved_claims.reason: Existing guide target/disposable-local-data, designated QA ownership, credential and auth boundaries govern bootstrap. Actual session/runtime availability is deliberately inspected during execution; unavailable prerequisites leave the lane pending. No new product decision or authorization needed at planning stage.

confidence.basis: Narrow founder-directed amendment, source-confirmed existing runtime step/usage limits and review with no retained gaps; target access and actual live proof remain execution prerequisites.
